title: cross-feed-observability-orchestrator-and-adaptive-slo-guards
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: We currently have disparate tracing hooks, metrics pipelines, and alerting policies owned by different squads. This causes noisy burn-rate alerts during traffic spikes, duplicated paging for the same underlying cause, and a lack of coordinated remediation when latency and error signals diverge across services.

Goal: Build a small orchestration layer and operator playbook that: 1) aligns sampling and enrichment decisions across SDKs and collectors (cross-feed tracing); 2) applies noise-aware SLO guards that adjust burn-rate thresholds using signal-correlation heuristics; 3) surfaces a unified incident summary and recommended paging target to reduce duplicate oncalls.

Scope: Prototype a coordinator service (stateless controller) that consumes sampled trace headers and metric fingerprints from the ingest pipeline, calculates correlated alert confidence, and emits an alert-decoration event consumed by the alert router. Deliverables: controller code, updated SDK hook spec, metrics pipeline enrichments, new dashboard panels, and an operations playbook for oncall.

Out of scope: Rewriting the whole tracing SDK; replacing existing alerting backend. This is an orchestration layer with minimal changes to existing agents and pipelines.
acceptance_criteria: Controller deployed to staging and can read ingest fingerprints from the observability Kafka topic
Controller produces alert-decoration event with correlated_confidence (low|medium|high) and suggested_pager (service|team) for >=80% of alerts in staging
Burn-rate alerts in staging respect the correlated_confidence (e.g., suppress or escalate) according to playbook
Runbook produced that documents how to interpret correlated_confidence, how to disable controller, and rollback steps
New dashboard panels show before/after alert volume, duplicate pager count, and mean time to acknowledgement (MTTA) for 2 weeks after rollout
implementation_steps: Design: finalize controller input schema and alert-decoration event payload (integration with existing alert router)
SDK: add optional sampling header propagation and lightweight fingerprint emit to collector agents
Ingest: enrich metrics pipeline to attach fingerprint and trace-id mapping to metrics batches
Controller: implement correlation heuristics (time-window join, tag overlap, adaptive thresholding) and confidence scoring
Alert Router Integration: consume decoration events and apply suppression/escalation policies based on confidence and runbook rules
Dashboards: create panels in Console showing correlated_confidence distribution and duplicate paging rate
Staging rollout: deploy controller to staging, enable opt-in teams, run chaos tests (traffic spikes, region failovers)
Canary: route 10% of production alerts through controller, monitor false suppressions, adjust heuristics
Full rollout: enable for platform services with SLOs and iterate
comments: 2026-02-26 Maya Chen: Spiked an initial design with Diego. Decided to keep controller stateless and rely on Kafka for joins to avoid new DB dependencies.

2026-03-03 Samira Patel (oncall): Ran local chaos test causing a burst of CPU errors; controller suppressed 12/40 duplicate pages in staging and attached correlated_confidence=high for the remaining ones — promising but two legitimate pages were suppressed, investigating threshold tuning.
2026-03-06 Product Review: PM notes - ensure playbook includes manual override steps and a visible kill-switch in Console. Also request metrics for false suppression rate.

2026-03-08 Diego Alvarez: Updated heuristics to add time-window decay and service-weighted tag matching. New staging runs show false suppression down from 5% to 1.1% in targeted tests. Preparing canary runbook.
